raw_segments.text: The sea in the neighborhood of the islands of Shetland is more than commonly abundant
in fish, which makes a great part of the subsistence of their inhabitants.
But in order to profit by the produce of the water, they must have a habitation upon the
The rent of the landlord is in proportion, not to what the farmer can make by the land,
but to what he can make both by the land and the water.
It is partly paid in sea fish, and one of the very few instances in which rent makes
a part of the price of that commodity is to be found in that country.
